newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak crown market nervous after foreign withdrawals.
newsitem.headline: Slovak crown market nervous after foreign withdrawals.

text.p: The Slovak crown recovered slightly in nervous Wednesday afternoon forex trading after morning foreign currency withdrawals by foreign banks pulled the currency one percentage point lower against its dollar/mark basket.

At 1350 GMT, the crown was trading on the interbank market at 31.063/079 to the dollar and 20.601/613 to the mark implying a depreciation against parity of 0.92 percent after hitting a 1.23 percent low at midday.
Dealers said an estimated $60-100 million left the country earlier in the day but the crown then stabilised after local banks bought currency from the central bank.
The central bank fixed the crown 1.0 percent below it's dollar/mark basket parity on Wednesday, having fixed it 0.5 percent below parity for more than a week.

"The situation has started to turn around a little but so far this (recovery) looks like a domestic bank initiative only and I fear now the index will fall further," Brano Matusek, a dealer at Tatra Banka, told Reuters.
"But the market is very nervous and I could just as quickly change my mind," Matusek added.
Added Peter Koprna of Slovenska Sporitelna: "It is hard to define the trend now, this morning could herald stormy days."
Tibor Fratrik, a forex dealer at ING Bank, said: "I only see larger movements in the coming days if the lower crown attracts foreign banks to re-open positions."
